rationale: SYS-1 is a beta-catenin-like coactivator in the Wnt/beta-catenin asymmetry pathway that directly controls asymmetric neuroblast divisions and diversification of sensory lineages. A missense variant in sys-1 could perturb asymmetric partitioning or transcriptional activation required for the AMso asymmetric division that produces an MCM neuron, leading to symmetric glial outcomes. This connection is supported by publications showing Wnt/beta-catenin asymmetry and SYS-1 involvement in asymmetric neuroblast divisions and cell-fate diversification [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 19389360, PMID 21917811, PMID 29962933].

Narrative: SYS-1 is a beta-catenin-like mediator of Wnt/beta-catenin asymmetry that directly controls asymmetric neuroblast divisions; a missense variant could impair SYS-1 function and block the AMso asymmetric division that produces MCM neurons, yielding two glia instead [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 19389360, PMID 21917811, PMID 29962933].

rationale: FEM-1 is part of the Cul2-RING ubiquitin ligase complex and is required for male germ-line and somatic sex determination. Disruption of fem-1 by a missense change could alter male-specific somatic patterning cues that instruct AMso reprogramming during male maturation, resulting in failure to produce MCM neurons and instead producing two glia [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].

Narrative: FEM-1 is part of a Cul2-RING ubiquitin ligase complex required for male somatic sex determination; a missense change may alter male-specific patterning signals necessary for AMso reprogramming during sexual maturation and thus prevent MCM production [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].

rationale: TDP-1/TDP-43 is an RNA-binding protein that regulates splicing and RNA metabolism in neurons. A splice-acceptor HIGH-impact variant is likely to cause strong loss-of-function or altered isoforms; altered RNA splicing in AMso or in upstream regulators could derail the transcriptional/post-transcriptional program required for the AMso asymmetric division and MCM specification. TDP-1 has extensive neuronal roles in C. elegans models of neurodegeneration, increasing the plausibility that its loss perturbs neural/glial fate programs [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, PMID 32531261, PMID 33963840].

rationale: TTR-13 is predicted to be a cell-surface/transthyretin-like protein; the splice-donor HIGH-impact variant could cause loss of function. If TTR-13 mediates extracellular signaling or cell-cell interactions required for AMso asymmetric division or for instructive male-specific cues, loss could shift the division outcome toward symmetric gliogenesis. The HIGH-impact splice_donor annotation increases prior probability despite limited functional annotation [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH].

rationale: ALG-1 is a core Argonaute in the miRNA pathway (RISC) and is required for developmental timing and neuronal regulation. miRNA regulation often controls cell-fate transitions and timing of differentiation; a missense change in alg-1 could impair miRNA-mediated repression needed for the AMso-to-MCM transition during male maturation. Several studies link ALG-1 functionality to neuronal development and developmental timing, supporting a mechanistic route to MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 29117550, PMID 24244204, PMID 23599497].

Chromatin regulators can control binary fate choices and lineage-specific transcription programs; a missense change could alter chromatin dynamics in AMso or in regulators of the AMso asymmetric division, mis-specifying fate and producing two glia instead of an MCM neuron [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].

Ubiquitin–deubiquitin systems and receptor trafficking can influence signaling thresholds that direct asymmetric divisions; a missense variant in wdr-48 could perturb stability of polarity or signaling components required for AMso reprogramming to MCM. Provided literature shows WDR-48 acts in neuronal receptor abundance and protein stability, supporting a plausible mechanism [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, PMID 33622778, PMID 32587090].
